newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers disturbed by low U.S. savings.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers disturbed by low U.S. savings.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Thursday lamented the low U.S. savings rate and said the administration was committed to working with Congress to boost it.
In prepared testimony to the Senate Finance Committee, Summers said the low individual savings rate was "particularly troubling" given the aging of the baby boom generation.
"Many families today have simply not accumulated the resources necessary to maintain their standard of living in retirement," Summers said.
He said that an increase in U.S. savings would likely have "beneficial effects" on economic growth, U.S. competitiveness and living standards.
To help bring that about, the administration is committed to eliminating the federal budget deficit, Summers said.
"I am confident that we can work together to achieve a balanced federal budget," he told the lawmakers.
Summers said the administration has also put forward ways to improve the effectiveness of Individual Retirement Accounts.
The administration's proposal would expand income limits, create new back-loaded IRAs, and eliminate the 10 percent early withdrawal tax for certain specific purposes.
